chunks: My father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim narrated to us from his father Ibrahim ibn Hashim from Abu Hudba.

He said: I saw that Anas ibn Malik was bound with a headband, so I asked him about it, and he said: This is [the result of] the supplication of Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him). So I said to him: How did that happen?

He said: I was a servant of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family). He was given a gift of a roasted bird, and he said: O Allah! Bring me the most beloved of Your creation to You and to me to eat from this bird with me.

So Ali (peace be upon him) came, and I said to him: The Messenger of Allah is too busy for you. And I wanted it to be a man from my own people. So the Messenger of Allah raised his hands a second time and said: O Allah! Bring me the most beloved of Your creation to You and to me to eat from this bird with me. So Ali (peace be upon him) came, and I said to him: The Messenger of Allah is too busy for you. And I wanted it to be a man from my own people. So the Messenger of Allah raised his hands a third time and said: O Allah! Bring me the most beloved of Your creation to You and to me to eat from this bird with me. So Ali (peace be upon him) came, and I said to him: The Messenger of Allah is too busy for you. And I wanted it to be a man from my own people.

So Ali (peace be upon him) raised his voice and said: What keeps the Messenger of Allah away from me? So the Messenger of Allah heard him and said: O Anas! Who is this? I said: Ali ibn Abi Talib. He said: Permit him [to enter]. When he entered, he said to him: O Ali! I have supplicated to God the Mighty and Majestic three times asking Him to bring me the most beloved of His creation to Him and to me to eat from this bird with me. Had you not come on the third time, I would have supplicated to God by your name asking Him to bring you to me.

So Ali (peace be upon him) said: O Messenger of Allah! I came three times. Each time Anas turned me away, saying: The Messenger of Allah is too busy for you. So the Messenger of Allah said to me: O Anas! What caused you to do this? I said: O Messenger of Allah! I heard the supplication and I wanted it to be a man from my own people.

When it was the Day of the Dar, Ali (peace be upon him) asked me to bear witness [to his appointment], but I concealed it and said: I have forgotten it. So Ali (peace be upon him) raised his hand toward the sky and said: O Allah! Afflict Anas with leprosy that he cannot hide from the people. Then he uncovered the headband from his head and said: This is the supplication of Ali, this is the supplication of Ali, this is the supplication of Ali.

key_terms.أَحَبُّ خَلْقِكَ: The most beloved of Your creation — the Prophet's supplication naming Ali indirectly
key_terms.الطَّائِرُ الْمَشْوِيُّ: The roasted bird — the occasion of this famous supplication
key_terms.الْوَضَحُ: Leprosy/vitiligo (literally 'whiteness') — the affliction that visibly struck Anas as punishment
key_terms.دَعْوَةُ عَلِيٍّ: The supplication of Ali — the proof of Ali's spiritual authority that Anas carries on his head
key_terms.يَوْمُ الدَّارِ: Day of the Dar — referring to the event where the Prophet publicly designated Ali as his successor (also associated with Ghadir or the gathering at Dar ibn Abi Talib)

ai.seo_question: What is the Hadith of the Roasted Bird (Hadith al-Ta'ir) and what does it say about Imam Ali's status?
ai.summary: This narrative, transmitted through al-Saduq's chain from Anas ibn Malik, recounts the famous incident known as Hadith al-Ta'ir (the Hadith of the Roasted Bird). The Prophet (SAWW) thrice prayed for the most beloved person to God and himself to share his meal, and each time Ali ibn Abi Talib (AS) appeared at the door, yet Anas turned him away hoping a man from his own tribe (the Ansar) would receive the honor. The hadith concludes with Ali's supplication against Anas for suppressing his testimony about the appointment at Yawm al-Dar, and Anas himself confirms this by showing the leprosy on his head, narrating the story as a form of remorseful confession. The narration powerfully illustrates Ali's unique spiritual station as the most beloved to both God and the Prophet.
